title: The Iron Road: Railways of Colonial India

narration.text: In 1853, the first passenger train in India left Bombay for Thane — sixteen kilometers that would bind a subcontinent together.

visual.description: Slow zoom on a vintage map of 1850s Bombay, sepia tones.

requirement.description: Historical map of Bombay region, 1850s, public domain.

narration.text: Within three decades, the network stretched from the coasts to the interior, carrying cotton, coal, and millions of travelers.

visual.description: Show archival railway footage from colonial India.

requirement.description: Archival footage of Indian railways, late 19th century.

narration.text: Bridges like the one over the Sutlej became symbols of an engineering ambition that outlived the empire.

visual.description: Wide shot of a colonial-era railway bridge over a wide river.

requirement.description: Period photograph of a stone railway bridge in India.

narration.text: For the people who built and rode these lines, the railway was neither symbol nor empire — it was daily life.

visual.description: Close, warm portrait-style still of travelers waiting on a platform.

narration.text: Today, that same iron road carries more than twenty million passengers a day.

visual.description: Modern busy railway platform, motion-blurred crowd, sunrise light.

requirement.description: Busy modern Indian railway platform at sunrise, crowds in motion.
